title: Enterprise Onboarding — Escalation, Integration, and QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Combined playbook for enterprise onboarding that codifies integration checklists, escalation procedures, known issues & workarounds, support process, and QBR / health-check templates to standardize customer handoffs and reduce time-to-value.
content:
Overview:
This playbook documents the standard operating procedures for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference, focusing on three linked areas: (1) Integration & launch checklist, (2) Escalation and support process, and (3) Health checks and Quarterly Business Review (QBR) templates. Use this doc as the canonical reference for CSMs, Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and Account Execs during the first 90–180 days of an enterprise customer relationship.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-production-call to <= 14 days for standard integrations.
- Ensure SLA-aware escalation with measurable handoff points and ownership.
- Provide consistent QBR materials and health metrics for renewal and upsell conversations.

Owner & Contacts:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success) — aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Primary escalation contact: Eng Support Lead, Marco Diaz — marco.diaz@redwood.ai
- Solutions Engineering: Evelyn Chen — evelyn.chen@redwood.ai

1) Integration & Launch Checklist (Pre-launch -> Go-live)
Intro: The checklist below should be completed and signed off by the CSM, SE, and customer technical lead. Each item maps to owner and acceptance criteria.

Pre-engagement (Sales -> CSM handoff):
1. PRD & success criteria collected and attached to the account workspace.
2. Contract & network requirements validated (VPC, IP allowlist, data residency).
3. Assign technical owners: CSM, SE, Oncall SRE.

Technical integration checklist (SE owner):
- API credentials provisioned and rotated (owner: customer, SE validates).
- Endpoint reachability validated from customer network (ping/curl test). Example command to validate connectivity:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
```

- Model & routing profile selected and pinned for initial traffic (model_id + version).
- Authentication & RBAC validated (SAML/OIDC/KMS integration if applicable).
- Request/response schema verified against sample payloads (include function-calling mappings).
- Latency and throughput smoke tests completed: 1000 synthetic requests at expected QPS or 5 minutes of production-like traffic.
- Traffic shaping and rate-limits configured (quota lanes established).
- Monitoring and alerting subscription added to customer workspace (errors, p50/p95 latency, token usage).
- Data handling & logs: ensure retention, PII scrubbing, and audit logging configuration meet contract.

Launch readiness sign-off (Checklist sign-off table):
- SE acceptance: "Integration smoke tests passed" — SE signature/email.
- CSM acceptance: "Business acceptance criteria met" — CSM signature.
- Legal/Security acceptance: "Compliance gates cleared" (if applicable).

2) Escalation & Support Process
Purpose: Provide a clear, time-bound escalation ladder with SLA targets and required artifacts for each escalation level.

Escalation levels (summary):
- Level 0: Customer self-service + docs/FAQ. Target first response: immediate via portal.
- Level 1 (Support Engineer): Triage incoming ticket. Target first response: < 2 hours (business hours).
- Level 2 (Senior Support / SE): Deep diagnosis, reproduce issue. Target takeover: < 4 hours.
- Level 3 (Eng / Runtime): Code-level or infra-level fix required. Target engagement: < 8 hours.
- Level 4 (Executive / Account): Business-impacting incidents requiring cross-org coordination. Target: notify within 1 business hour of escalation.

Escalation matrix (owners & contact points):
- Customer Success (CSM): Primary liaison for business impact and QBRs.
- Support (Level 1/2): support@redwood.ai or portal ticket.
- Solutions Eng (Level 2): escalation@redwood.ai (SE queue).
- Runtime Eng (Level 3): oncall-runtime@redwood.ai (pager duty).
- Security Incidents: sec-incident@redwood.ai (follow SecOps runbook).

Required artifacts when escalating:
1. Customer name, environment (prod/staging), and account ID.
2. Exact timestamp(s) of observed failure and request IDs (if available).
3. Reproduction steps and minimum request payload that fails.
4. Logs (redacted for PII) and correlation IDs.
5. Impact statement: number of users affected, business impact, suggested priority.

Escalation procedure (numbered steps):
1. Level 1 receives ticket, acknowledges within 2 hours and collects artifacts.
2. If not resolvable within 4 hours, escalate to Level 2 with artifacts attached.
3. Level 2 reproduces and attempts mitigation or rollback. If fix requires runtime changes, escalate to Level 3.
4. For Sev-1 (production outage affecting >50% of requests), immediately page Level 3 and notify CSM and Account Exec.
5. Post-incident: run RCA and customer-facing postmortem within 72 hours for Sev-1/Sev-2.

Support SLAs (example):
- Sev-1 (system outage): initial response 15 minutes, mitigation/update every 30 minutes until resolved.
- Sev-2 (significant feature degradation): initial response 1 hour, updates every 2 hours.
- Sev-3 (partial loss / minor bug): initial response 4 hours, daily updates.

3) Known Issues & Workarounds (Customer-facing summary)
Purpose: Maintain a curated list of known issues relevant to enterprise customers with reproducible steps, impact, workaround, and ETA for fix. Update the account workspace and link to public KB article when appropriate.

Table: Known issues (example rows)
| ID | Symptom | Impact | Workaround | ETA | Owner |
|----|---------|--------|-----------|-----|-------|
| KI-2026-011 | Intermittent 503 on long-sequence requests | Some requests for long-context > 8k tokens fail | Reduce max_tokens to 4k or route to high-memory pool; enable streaming retries | Rolling fix in runtime 2026-10-07 | Runtime Eng |
| KI-2026-018 | Embedding mismatch after quantized model rollout | Up to 4% embedding drift for specific vector indexers | Pin previous model version for similarity queries until re-embedding completed | Hotfix planned 2026-10-01 | Model Onboarding |

When to publish an issue to KB:
- If workaround is customer-actionable and affects >1 customer, publish public KB with guidance.
- For sensitive security issues, follow Security classification and keep details restricted until coordinated release.

4) Health Checks & QBR Materials
Objective: Provide a set of operational and product health indicators to track adoption, detect regressions, and inform QBR discussions.

Core health metrics (CSM dashboard):
- Adoption: active routes per week, unique callers, tokens per day. Target growth: +10% MoM first 3 months.
- Performance: p50/p95 latency, error rate (5xx/4xx), and Uptime (target 99.95% for Dedicated customers).
- Cost efficiency: avg tokens per successful response, cache hit rate, batch utilization.
- Quality: user-reported accuracy issues, eval spike counts, regression test pass rate.

Health check cadence:
- Week 1–4: weekly operational review (CSM + SE) to resolve integration gaps.
- Week 4–12: bi-weekly health check focusing on optimization and cost controls.
- Quarterly: QBR with exec summary, adoption, ROI, roadmap alignment.

QBR template (slide structure):
1. Executive summary (1 slide): current health, top wins, top risks.
2. Usage & Adoption (1–2 slides): volume trends, top routes, cost/benefit.
3. Performance & Reliability (1 slide): latency, errors, recent incidents and mitigations.
4. Quality & Product (1 slide): model performance, user feedback, open regressions.
5. Roadmap & Next Steps (1 slide): planned improvements, feature requests, timelines.
6. Ask & Decisions (1 slide): items requiring customer approval or commercial changes.

QBR preparation checklist:
- Collect last 90 days of metrics and highlight top 3 trends.
- Confirm any open escalations and status.
- Draft recommendations for cost/perf optimizations (e.g., quantization, batching, cache tuning).
- Share the deck with customer and internal reviewers 5 business days before QBR.

5) Post-incident & Post-onboarding Reviews
- For any Sev-1/Sev-2 incident during onboarding, the CSM + SE schedule a customer postmortem within 72 hours.
- Within 30 days of go-live, run a "30-day onboarding review" to capture lessons learned and update playbook.
- Capture action items in the account workspace and assign ownership with due dates.

6) Templates & Artifacts (links and examples)
- Integration runbook template: attach JSON/YAML for sample request/response and allowed headers.
- Escalation email template: subject, summary of impact, required artifacts.
- QBR deck template: downloadable slide deck (internal).
- KB article template for publishing known issues.

Appendix A — Example Escalation Email Template:
Subject: [Escalation] {Customer} {Account ID} — {Short symptom} — {Severity}
Body:
1) Summary of impact
2) Customer environment & steps to reproduce
3) Correlation IDs / timestamps
4) Business impact & requested priority
5) Attach logs / screenshots / sample payload

Appendix B — Troubleshooting quick commands:
- Check API health:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq
```
- Retrieve recent request logs (SE support CLI):
```
redwood logs list --account <ACCOUNT_ID> --limit 200 --filter "status>=500"
```

Governance & Change Control:
- Any change to SLA targets, escalation SLAs, or QBR cadence must be approved by Director of Customer Success and Head of Support.
- Playbook review cadence: quarterly. Critical postmortem actions that change procedures must be reflected here within 14 days.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ):
Q: When should I escalate directly to Runtime Eng?
A: If a reproducible failure requires changes to the serving runtime (kernel or scheduling), or if a Sev-1 outage is detected, page Runtime Eng per the matrix.

Q: How do we handle PII in logs shared with Engineering?
A: Remove or redact PII before attaching logs. Use the anonymization script in the SE toolkit and mark the ticket as "redacted logs attached."
